content.text:
The polish pass is done and verified end-to-end in the browser. `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint over all 23 changed files, and `npm run build` are all clean, and I walked the live flow (login → OTP → profile picker → home → visits → records → prescription detail → profile → switcher → booking) against the design frames.

## The two root causes

**`bg-primary-50` painted nothing.** The repo's Tailwind `primary` palette starts at `100`, so all 34 `bg-primary-50` usages resolved to transparent — every tinted "selected"/"upcoming" surface in the design was silently flat. Adding the missing step to [tailwind.config.js](tailwind.config.js) is what makes the selected profile card, the switcher's active row, the switch confirmation strip, and the visit-summary icon tiles read as tinted. This also fixes ~20 staff-facing usages outside the portal — worth knowing before you merge.

**Status pills had no small size.** The shared `Badge` bottoms out around 24px; the design's are 18px. Since `src/components/ui/` is off-limits, I added [PatientBadge.tsx](src/components/Patient/PatientBadge.tsx) with tones named by meaning, which also retired the off-palette blue "Booked" chip on the visits list.

## What the seven agents changed

Header chip moved left with the `VIEWING` eyebrow and a semantic avatar (primary fill = who you're viewing, neutral = everyone else); the switcher's stray X is gone, leaving the grabber; quick actions went from three-line wrapped tiles to the design's compact 4-up; filter chips, section labels, and card padding tightened throughout; visit statuses map onto real tones; the profile's account row shows the owner's name instead of an avatar reading "09"; the booking wizard collapsed to a single header row and now reports "Step 1 of 4" so the progress bar actually fills.

## Four judgment calls I made against the mock

- **Kept the configurable logo.** An agent had replaced `careConfig.mainLogo` with a hardcoded "care." lockup. CARE is white-label — I took the design's 38px scale and left the mark to the deployment.
- **Dropped "A unit of the State Health Department."** Deployment-specific copy; the configured helpline is the only thing worth pinning.
- **No notification bell.** The design has one, but there's no notifications feature behind it — a fake control.
- **Prescription list cards stay compact.** An agent left a rich card with an empty band where medicines belong; the list endpoint only returns them on the detail request, so I collapsed it to the design's compact row rather than ship a hole.

Also worth flagging: the profile footer renders the build id, which is a UUID here, not the mock's "v3.2" — I truncated it to 8 chars so it stays quotable to support without running across the footer. And I couldn't verify the report-detail and visit-summary screens visually because this patient has no diagnostic reports and no completed visit; those two rest on typecheck and code review only.

All five items are implemented and verified in the running app. One thing to flag first: an **Entire checkpoint hook auto-committed** mid-session as `9a562b1e1 "More clean up"` — I didn't run any git commands, that's the repo's own automation. My last three files are still uncommitted on top of it.

**1. Care logo restored.** Home leads with `careConfig.mainLogo` again and the `VIEWING` chip moved back to the trailing slot. The design's chip-left/bell-right arrangement lost the only branded surface in the portal, and you're right that identity beats the mock here.

**2. Actions off the list cards.** Both the home card and the Visits upcoming card are now a single tappable card — no Reschedule/Cancel — and the space went to appointment data instead: session name, slot time range, facility. Reschedule and Cancel now live on the visit screen, where the whole appointment is in front of you. Reschedule is also gated to upcoming visits now, and Cancel is a quiet ghost link rather than a full button.

**3. Home lists prescriptions, not medicines.** The old preview fanned out one detail request per prescription just to flatten their medicines into a list where you couldn't tell which visit a medicine came from. It now renders prescriptions and drops those N extra requests. I extracted [PrescriptionRow.tsx](src/components/Patient/PrescriptionRow.tsx) so home and the Records list are literally the same row — that's the "Rx listed nicely" part.

**4 & 5. The pass.** New [AppointmentTokenPass.tsx](src/components/Patient/AppointmentTokenPass.tsx), modelled on your screenshot: patient name/age/gender, practitioner, session + date + time range, facility, token number, QR. The Success page and the visit screen now render the identical component, so what you see when you book is what you find again later — the success route being unreachable afterwards is fixed. It shows while the appointment is still open (through check-in) and disappears once the visit is fulfilled or cancelled, where a past-visit card with Facility/Session/Token/Booked on/Reason takes over instead. Verified both states: the upcoming Aug 1 booking shows the pass, the fulfilled Jul 31 visit shows the summary card.

**One judgment call worth your review:** you asked for a QR "in that part" where the appointment id was. The QR encodes the **patient id**, not the appointment id — that's what `PatientIDScanDialog` and both staff token cards already speak, so a counter scanner resolves it straight to the patient. The appointment id is still shown, shortened to an 8-character booking reference so it reads as a reference rather than a raw UUID. If you'd rather the QR carry the appointment id, that's a one-line change.

`tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, and `npm run build` are clean.
